gaps.sentence: She told me ___ had happened, but I didn't believe her.
gaps.explanation: 'What had happened' means 'the things that had happened'; 'that' cannot stand alone as the subject here.

gaps.sentence: There are times ___ I really miss my home town.
gaps.explanation: 'There are times when ...' is a standard pattern; 'when' stands for 'at which'.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: There is nothing ___ I would change about the design.
gaps.explanation: After 'nothing', use 'that' (or omit the pronoun); 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: Mount Everest, ___ was first climbed in 1953, attracts hundreds of climbers every year.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces extra information about the mountain; 'that' is wrong after a comma.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: He is a colleague on ___ you can always depend.
gaps.explanation: After 'on', the formal relative pronoun for a person is 'whom'.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.
